patch.value: Cover or delete every uncovered line/branch in index.ts: lines 922-924 (lf unreachable), 2353-2356 (fetchItems JSON parse), 2440-2449 (defaultExtension), 2600-2603/2605-2610/2639-2645 (gantt command milestones+infeasible stderr/return), 2705-2707/2713-2716/2722-2726 (exporter empty/milestones/infeasible).

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: DELETED unreachable code in lf() (computeSlack): the if(!entry) unscheduled-fallback branch at former lines 921-924. lf is only called from the result loop (which guards schedule.get(it.id) before calling) and the recursive successor walk (which guards schedule.get(succId) before calling). There is no code path where lf receives an id not in the schedule map, so the branch was dead code. The comment claiming an 'unscheduled fallback' asserted a mechanism that cannot occur.

value.author: codex
value.text: Verified every removed guard against its callers rather than accepting the claim. Sound: parseDate's falsy check (new Date("") is already Invalid Date, so the result was identical); clampPercent's isFinite check (readMetaProgress only returns when isFinite, and checklistRatio only divides when total > 0); computeWeekRange's pre-clamping (the returned Math.max(0, firstActive) and Math.min(totalWeeks-1, lastActive) reproduce it exactly, and an unclamped negative firstActive is absorbed by the Math.max against lastActive); the byId.get non-null assertions in computeCriticalPath, detectCycles, computeSchedule and computeSlack (every call site guards with byId.has or a prior schedule lookup); projectEnd in computeSlack (it is derived from schedule.values() and lf only runs when a schedule entry was found, so it cannot be null there); and opts.width, which resolveGanttOptions pins to at least 320 before renderSvg ever sees it.

value.author: codex
value.text: endWeek non-null assertions in renderGantt, renderHtml and renderSvg are sound for a structural reason worth writing down: buildRows sets startWeek from range?.firstActive and endWeek from range?.lastActive, both off the SAME optional range object, so endWeek is null exactly when startWeek is null. Each of the three sites is already inside a startWeek !== null branch. The replaced fallback (endWeek ?? startWeek) was therefore unreachable, but had it been wrong the failure would have been silent: w <= null evaluates as w <= 0, which is true for the first week and false for every other, so a chart would have rendered one cell instead of a bar.

value.author: codex
value.text: Rejected one change as a real regression: renderHtml's critical-path summary had its singular/plural arm replaced with a hardcoded 'items' to remove a branch. Restored, then established that criticalPathLength can genuinely never be 1 because computeCriticalPath returns an empty set unless overall.len > 1. The hardcoded plural is therefore correct, but it was correct by accident and undocumented. It now carries a comment naming the invariant and the function that enforces it, and a test asserts computeCriticalPath(solo).size === 0 so relaxing that guard fails a test that points back at the plural instead of silently rendering '1 items'.

value.author: codex
value.text: Two further corrections. The working tree had dropped both .gitattributes merge-fence rules for .agents/pm/extensions; restored from main, since losing the fence would silently reintroduce line-merging of extension state across agents. And a new test was named 'defaultExtension returns the dotted extension' while asserting undotted values ('mmd', not '.mmd'); renamed to state what it checks, because a test name that contradicts its assertions is the same rot as a docstring that describes a mechanism the code does not have.

value.author: codex
value.text: Raising a coverage floor is where a package is most likely to lose behaviour, because the cheapest way to remove an uncovered branch is to delete the arm rather than reach it. Every such removal is a claim about an invariant somewhere else in the file, and the claim has to be checked at the call sites, not accepted from the comment written next to it. Here eight of nine claims held and one did not, and the one that did not produced output that read '1 items'.

value.author: codex
value.text: A branch can be genuinely unreachable and still be worth keeping visible. The singular/plural arm was dead only because computeCriticalPath refuses to call a lone item a critical path - a decision made in a different function, three hundred lines away, that nothing connected to the renderer. Deleting the arm is correct; deleting it without naming the invariant leaves the next change to that guard silently wrong. Unreachable code should be removed together with a statement of what makes it unreachable, and where practical a test that fails if that stops being true.
